chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskān, from Al-Ḥalabī, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: Abū 'Abdillāh: A title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.اَلْأَنْفَالِ: Anfal: Plural of nafilah, referring to public treasury, state assets, or surplus wealth in Islamic jurisprudence.
key_terms.مَوْلًى: Mawlā: A guardian, patron, or heir from the clan/tribe, often referring to the client of a tribe or the Imam in Shia jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the estate of a deceased person who has no heirs or mawla?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the application of Quranic verse 8:1, specifying that 'anfal' in the context of inheritance refers to the property of one who dies without a 'mawlā' (client or tribal guardian). In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes the Imam's right to inherit from such individuals, distinguishing this category from those with distant relatives (dhawi al-arham) who may receive a share but do not transfer full ownership to the state treasury.
